title: Transcriber's Note Regarding Omitting a Print Symbol

illustrates.quote: i. When the table uses only one type of symbol or abbreviation, omit it from all entries in the table. Explain the omission in a transcriber's note placed before the table. Sample: All numbers in the table are percentages. (See Sample 11-14: Transcriber's Note Regarding Omitting a Print Symbol on page 11-39.)

print.caption: Table 16 / Long-Term Trends in Grade 12
rows: Half pack or more per day
print.notes: "Cigarettes" is a cell-5-style group heading with no entries of its own; "Daily" and "Half pack or more per day" are the actual data rows, every entry being a percentage.
print.printFeatures: Bordered box; the title ("Table 16" / "Long-Term Trends in Grade 12", bold, centred) is INSIDE the box at the top, above a ruled line; header row (years) with ruled line beneath; the group heading "Cigarettes" stands alone in its row, with the two data rows indented beneath it.

braille.notes: A transcriber's note (lines 7-8) explains: "All figures 9 [in] table >e [are] p]c5tages [percentages]." ("All figures in table are percentages.") — matching rule 11.7.1.i's sample wording almost exactly. As a result, the '%' sign is omitted from every entry in the table body (lines 13, 15) since it is the table's one and only recurring symbol.
